mainTopic: Wondrous travel stories: רבה בר בר חנה's desert journeys with the Arab, and the sea stories of רבי יוחנן and רב ספרא
overview: This amud is full of wondrous travel stories. רבה בר בר חנה, guided by an Arab, sees the giant bodies of the מתי מדבר and cuts a corner of one man's תכלת, but he cannot move until he gives it back. The רבנן scold him, since he could have settled the ציצית question just by counting the threads. At הר סיני he hears a בת קול regretting an oath, and the רבנן fault him for not cancelling it. The גמרא explains that he feared it was the oath about the מבול, and the רבנן answer that God would not say "woe is Me" about that oath. He then hears קרח's swallowed followers confess that משה and his תורה are true, and he loses his basket where the earth and sky meet, until he learns the turning sky will bring it back. Next come sea stories: רבי יוחנן's giant fish, and רב ספרא's horned fish, which רב אשי identifies as the goat of the sea. The amud ends as רבי יוחנן begins a story about a jeweled crate guarded by sharks, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The giants lying in the desert
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה describes the dead of the מתי מדבר lying on their backs. They are so huge that an Arab on a camel, holding his spear upright, rides under one raised knee without touching it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were lying on their backs. One of them had his knee raised, and the Arab rode under his knee on a camel with his spear held straight up, and he did not touch it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of the מתי מדבר continues. רבה בר בר חנה describes how enormous their bodies were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The image shows their size. A man on a camel, with a spear pointing upward, fits under a single raised knee. This sets the scene for what happens next.

keyTerms.meaning: An Arab merchant or traveler (his guide)

phrases.english: And they were lying on their backs.
phrases.notes: "They" are the מתי מדבר, the generation that died in the desert.

phrases.english: And the knee of one of them was raised,
and the Arab went in under his knee
while riding a camel,
with his spear held upright, and he did not touch him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the מתי מדבר from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bodies of the מתי מדבר are huge: a rider on a camel with an upright spear passes under one knee.

steps.title: Cutting the corner of the ציצית and returning it
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה cuts a corner of תכלת from one of the dead. He and the Arab then cannot move until he returns it.
steps.simpleTranslation: I cut off one corner of the תכלת garment of one of them, and we could not move. The Arab said: Maybe you took something from them? Give it back, because we have a tradition that whoever takes something from them cannot move. I went and gave it back, and then we could move.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. Taking something from the dead stops the travelers in their tracks, and giving it back frees them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Arab explains this with a known tradition: whoever takes from the מתי מדבר cannot move on. Once the corner is returned, they can move again. This act is what the רבנן will criticize in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: תכלת, the blue-dyed garment or thread of ציצית
Able to walk or move along

phrases.english: I cut off one corner of the sky-blue garment
of one of them,
and we were unable to move.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: דִּלְמָא שְׁקַלְתְּ מִידֵּי מִינַּיְיהוּ?
phrases.english: He said to me: Perhaps you took something from them?
Return it,
for we have a tradition that whoever takes something from them
cannot move.
I went and returned it,
and then we were able to move again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same scene with the giants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever takes something from the מתי מדבר cannot move until he returns it.

steps.title: The Sages scold him: just count the threads
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן call him a fool. If he wanted to settle the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about ציצית, he only had to count the threads and joints, not cut a piece off.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came before the רבנן they said to me: Every אבא is a donkey and every בר בר חנה is a fool! For what הלכה did you do that? To find out whether the הלכה follows בית שמאי or בית הלל? You should have counted the threads and counted the joints.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן attack what רבה בר בר חנה did. Cutting the corner was pointless, because there was a simpler way to learn the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן guess his reason: he wanted to see how the ancient ציצית were made, to settle the debate between בית שמאי and בית הלל. Counting the strings and windings on the spot would have answered that, so taking anything was unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Joints, the groups of windings on the ציצית

steps.whyThisMatters: This same rebuke comes back in step 5, so it works like a refrain in these stories.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּנַן, אֲמַרוּ לִי:
phrases.english: When I came before the Sages, they said to me:
Every Abba is a donkey,
phrases.notes: They are teasing him by using his own name.

phrases.english: and every bar bar Chana is an idiot!
For what הלכה did you do this?

phrases.aramaic: לְמִידַּע אִי כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי אִי כְּבֵית הִלֵּל?
phrases.english: To know whether it follows בית שמאי or בית הלל?
phrases.notes: They argue about how many threads go into ציצית.

phrases.aramaic: אִיבְּעִי לָךְ לְמִימְנֵי חוּטִין וּלְמִימְנֵי חוּלְיוֹת.
phrases.english: You should have counted the threads and counted the joints.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּנַן, אֲמַרוּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Criticizes the act described in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: His cutting off the corner of the תכלת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whatever הלכה he hoped to learn could have been learned by counting on the spot, so taking the corner was needless.

steps.title: הר סיני and the בת קול regretting an oath
steps.stepSummary: The Arab shows him הר סיני, surrounded by scorpions as big as white donkeys. He hears a בת קול say: Woe is Me that I swore, and now who will cancel it for Me?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Come, I will show you הר סיני. I went and saw scorpions surrounding it, standing as tall as white donkeys. I heard a בת קול saying: Woe is Me that I swore! Now that I have sworn, who will cancel it for Me?
steps.whatsHappening: A new scene begins on the same journey. At הר סיני, רבה בר בר חנה hears a heavenly voice regretting an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בת קול speaks for הקב"ה, regretting an oath and asking who can cancel it. The voice does not say which oath it means. That open question drives the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לִי: תָּא אַחְוֵי לָךְ הַר סִינַי.
phrases.english: He said to me: Come, I will show you Mount Sinai.
I went and saw that scorpions surrounded it,
and they stood like white donkeys.
phrases.notes: He means they were as tall as white donkeys.

phrases.english: I heard a Divine Voice saying:
"Woe is Me that I swore;
and now that I have sworn, who will cancel it for Me?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לִי: תָּא אַחְוֵי לָךְ הַר סִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new scene on the same journey with the Arab.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בת קול at הר סיני regrets an oath and asks who will cancel it.

steps.title: The Sages scold him: you should have cancelled it
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן repeat their insult. He should have answered the בת קול with "מופר לך", "it is cancelled for you."
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came before the רבנן they said to me: Every אבא is a donkey and every בר בר חנה is a fool! You should have said: It is cancelled for you!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן criticize him a second time. This time they fault him for doing nothing when he heard the בת קול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בת קול asked who would cancel the oath, so the רבנן say he should have cancelled it himself by saying "מופר לך". The same insult from step 3 is repeated here.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is cancelled for you," the words used to undo a vow or oath

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּנַן, אֲמַרוּ לִי:
phrases.english: When I came before the Sages, they said to me:
Every Abba is a donkey,
every bar bar Chana is an idiot!
You should have said: "It is cancelled for you!"

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּנַן, אֲמַרוּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the בת קול scene in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: His silence when the בת קול asked who would cancel the oath
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The voice asked for someone to cancel the oath, so he should have done it.

steps.title: Why he held back: maybe it was the oath about the מבול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains his reasoning. He worried the oath might be the promise never to bring another מבול, which should not be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he thought: Perhaps it is the oath about the flood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now defends רבה בר בר חנה against the רבנן's criticism.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The voice never said which oath it meant. If it was the oath not to flood the world again, cancelling it would be a disaster, so he was afraid to act.

keyTerms.meaning: The oath not to bring another flood

phrases.english: And he reasoned:
Perhaps it is the oath about the flood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's criticism in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reasoning behind his silence
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He simply failed to act when he should have.
steps.terutzMaskana: He held back on purpose, afraid it might be the oath against another flood.

steps.title: The Sages answer: then why "woe is Me"?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject his worry. If it were the oath against a flood, הקב"ה would not say "woe is Me" about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? If so, why say "woe is Me"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's reply, which pushes aside רבה בר בר חנה's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath against a flood is a kind promise, so there is nothing to regret about it. Since the voice said "woe is Me," it must be a different oath, and he should have cancelled it.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן fault רבה בר בר חנה twice: cutting the ציצית was pointless, and he should have cancelled the oath. His defense, that it might be the flood oath, fails because a good oath would not cause regret.

phrases.english: And the Sages: If so,
why "woe is Me"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense given in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the oath was the oath about the flood
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An oath that protects the world gives no reason to regret it, yet the voice said "woe is Me."
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רבנן hold that the oath was one הקב"ה regretted, so רבה בר בר חנה should have cancelled it.

steps.title: The smoking cracks of Korach's swallowed people
steps.stepSummary: The Arab shows רבה בר בר חנה two smoking cracks in the ground where קרח's followers were swallowed. Wet wool on a spear comes out scorched.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Come, I will show you the people of קרח who were swallowed. I saw two cracks in the ground giving off smoke. He took a tuft of wool, soaked it in water, stuck it on the tip of a spear and put it in there. When he took it out, it was completely scorched.
steps.whatsHappening: The Arab guide shows רבה בר בר חנה a new wonder: the place where the earth swallowed קרח and his group. A wet piece of wool put inside comes out burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new episode in the same chain of stories, so nothing earlier is being challenged. Soaking the wool in water first shows how intense the heat is: even wet wool gets burned. This sets up the next scene, where they hear the voices from below.

keyTerms.meaning: Those swallowed with קרח: the people the earth swallowed in the desert
Cracks or openings in the ground

phrases.english: He said to me: Come, I will show you
those swallowed with Korach.
I saw two cracks in the ground,
and they were giving off smoke.
He took a tuft of wool
and soaked it in water,
and stuck it on the tip of a spear
and put it in there,
and when he took it out, it was completely scorched.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִי: תָּא אַחְוֵי לָךְ בְּלוּעֵי דְקֹרַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the episode at הר סיני, the Arab guide moves on to a new wonder.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The guide shows the opening where קרח's group was swallowed. Its heat scorches even wet wool.

steps.title: The voices admit that משה is true
steps.stepSummary: The guide tells him to listen, and he hears the swallowed people saying: משה and his תורה are true, and we are liars.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Listen, what do you hear? And I heard them saying: 'משה and his תורה are true, and they are liars.'
steps.whatsHappening: Standing by the cracks, רבה בר בר חנה hears the swallowed people of קרח admit that משה was right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרח had challenged משה's leadership. Now his followers openly admit that משה and his תורה are true and that they themselves were the liars. The story turns the scene of punishment into a confession.

keyTerms.meaning: משה and his תורה are true
Liars, people who made things up

steps.confusionAlert: 'And they are liars' does not refer to someone else. The speakers mean themselves, but they say 'they' instead of 'we' to avoid calling themselves liars directly.

phrases.english: He said to me: Listen, what do you hear?
And I heard that they were saying:
"Moshe and his Torah are true,
and they are liars."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues at the same smoking cracks and adds what can be heard there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The swallowed people of קרח declare that משה and his תורה are true and that they were the liars.

steps.title: Every thirty days they are turned back here
steps.stepSummary: The guide explains that every thirty days גיהנם churns them back to this spot like meat in a pot, and each time they repeat the same confession.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Every thirty days גיהנם turns them back to here, like meat in a pot, and they say this: 'משה and his תורה are true, and they are liars.'
steps.whatsHappening: The guide explains why the voices can be heard at this spot: once every thirty days they are brought back here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat in a boiling pot keeps rising and sinking. In the same way, the swallowed people are carried around in גיהנם and come back to this opening every thirty days. Each time they come back, they repeat the same admission.

keyTerms.meaning: Like meat in a pot, which keeps moving around as it boils

steps.whatToRemember: The story of קרח's swallowed followers ends with a repeated confession: משה and his תורה are true.

phrases.english: He said to me: Every thirty days
Gehinnom turns them back to here
like meat in a pot,
phrases.notes: Picture meat bobbing up and down in a boiling pot. That's how they keep getting carried around.

phrases.english: and they say this:
"Moshe and his Torah are true, and they are liars."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לִי: כֹּל תְּלָתִין יוֹמֵי מַהְדַּר לְהוּ גֵּיהִנָּם לְהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how often the voices from step 9 return to this spot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every thirty days they return to this opening and repeat the confession.

steps.title: Where the earth and sky meet, and the basket disappears
steps.stepSummary: The guide shows him where the earth and sky touch. רבה בר בר חנה puts his basket in a 'window' of the sky, and after he prays it is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Come, I will show you where the earth and the sky kiss each other. I took my basket and put it in a window of the sky. After I finished praying, I looked for it and didn't find it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new wonder begins: the place where earth and sky touch. The basket vanishing sets up the question and answer that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story pictures the sky as a dome that reaches down and meets the earth at the edges, with openings ('windows') in it. The basket disappears into one of them, and the next two steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: The earth and the sky 'kiss', meaning they touch

phrases.english: He said to me: Come, I will show you
where the earth and the sky kiss each other.
I took my basket,
and put it in a window of the sky.
After I finished praying,
I looked for it and did not find it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִי: תָּא אַחְוֵי לָךְ הֵיכָא דְּנָשְׁקִי אַרְעָא וּרְקִיעָא אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new episode with the same guide.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the place where earth and sky meet, his basket disappears.

steps.title: Are there thieves here?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה asks the guide whether thieves took his basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: Are there thieves here?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה gives the obvious guess, that someone stole his basket. This question sets up the guide's surprising explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question looking for information: what happened to the basket? The natural guess is theft, and the answer will replace that guess with a cosmic explanation.

phrases.english: I said to him: Are there thieves here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the basket disappearing in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happened to the basket? Was it stolen?

steps.title: The turning sky carried it away
steps.stepSummary: The guide explains that the sky's wheel turns. If he waits until tomorrow, the basket will come back around.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: This is the wheel of the sky that turned around. Wait here until tomorrow and you will find it.
steps.whatsHappening: The guide answers that no one stole the basket. The sky turned and carried it away, and it will come back by tomorrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sky is described as a wheel that makes a full turn every day. The basket was carried along by the turning sky, so after one full day it will return to the same place.
steps.whatToRemember: The basket was not stolen. The turning sky carried it away, and it would return after one full day.

phrases.english: He said to me: This is the wheel of the sky
that turned around;
wait here until tomorrow,
and you will find it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לִי: הַאי גִּלְגְּלָא דִרְקִיעָא הֲוָה דְּהָדַר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No thieves took it. The turning sky carried the basket away, and it will return tomorrow.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's giant fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells of a fish whose eyes looked like two moons and whose gills sprayed water like two rivers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן relates: Once we were traveling on a ship, and we saw a fish that put its head out of the sea. Its eyes looked like two moons, and water sprayed from its two gills like the two rivers of סורא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from רבה בר בר חנה's stories to a new set of sea stories, starting with one told by רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new series of stories by a different teller. The point is the fish's enormous size: its eyes are compared to moons, and the water from its gills to whole rivers.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan relates:

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָא אָזְלִינַן בִּסְפִינְתָּא;
phrases.english: Once we were traveling on a ship;
and we saw a certain fish
that put its head out of the sea,
and its eyes looked like two moons;
and water sprayed from its two gills
like the two rivers of Sura.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשְׁתַּעֵי: זִימְנָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָא אָזְלִינַן בִּסְפִינְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבה בר בר חנה's stories to a new teller and a new series of sea stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן saw a fish of enormous size.

steps.title: רב ספרא's horned fish heading into the Leviathan's mouth
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא tells of a horned fish inscribed 'I am a lowly creature of the sea', three hundred פרסאות long, on its way into the לויתן's mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא relates: Once we were traveling on a ship, and we saw a fish that put its head out of the sea. It had horns, and engraved on it was: 'I am a lowly creature of the sea, I am three hundred פרסאות long, and I am going into the mouth of the לויתן.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא tells a story that opens with the same words as רבי יוחנן's, about an even stranger fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The creature is enormous, three hundred פרסאות long, yet it calls itself 'lowly'. It is food for the לויתן, which shows how much bigger the לויתן must be.

keyTerms.meaning: פרסאות, a long measure of distance
The לויתן, a giant sea creature

phrases.english: Rav Safra relates:

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָא אָזְלִינַן בִּסְפִינְתָּא;
phrases.english: Once we were traveling on a ship;
and we saw a certain fish
that put its head out of the sea,
and it had horns
and engraved on it was:
"I am a lowly creature of the sea";
and I am three hundred parsa'os long,
phrases.notes: The engraving is still speaking here. The fish is describing its own size.

phrases.english: and I am going into the mouth of the Leviathan.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָפְרָא מִשְׁתַּעֵי: זִימְנָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָא אָזְלִינַן בִּסְפִינְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second sea story that uses the same opening words as רבי יוחנן's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A huge horned fish calls itself lowly because it is food for the לויתן.

steps.title: רב אשי identifies the horned creature
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the creature רב ספרא saw was the 'goat of the sea', which searches through the sea and has horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That is the goat of the sea, which searches through the sea and has horns.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tells us what kind of creature רב ספרא saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי gives the creature a name, 'goat of the sea'. The horns fit the name, and he adds that it searches through the sea. He adds new information about the story without challenging it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
That is the goat of the sea,
which searches through the sea and has horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָהוּא עִיזָּא דְיַמָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the creature described in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The horned creature was the 'goat of the sea'.

steps.title: A jeweled crate guarded by sharks
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells of a crate set with precious stones and pearls, surrounded by sharks. The story begins with someone going down to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן relates: Once we were traveling on a ship, and we saw a crate set with precious stones and pearls, and a kind of fish called sharks surrounded it. He went down...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן begins another sea story about a treasure crate guarded by sharks. Someone goes down to it, and the story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a new scene: a treasure, and dangerous fish guarding it. The last word, 'he went down', starts the action, so this step leaves us waiting to hear what happens next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan relates:

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָא אָזְלִינַן בִּסְפִינְתָּא;
phrases.english: Once we were traveling on a ship;
and we saw a certain crate,

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲווֹ קָא מְקַבְּעִי בַּהּ אֲבָנִים טוֹבוֹת וּמַרְגָּלִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: in which precious stones and pearls were set,
and a kind of fish surrounded it
that is called sharks.
He went down

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשְׁתַּעֵי: זִימְנָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָא אָזְלִינַן בִּסְפִינְתָּא; וַחֲזֵינַן הָהִיא קַרְטְלִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new sea story by רבי יוחנן, after the horned fish episode ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A jeweled crate is guarded by sharks, and someone goes down toward it.
